newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala counts tickets in stadium tragedy probe.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala counts tickets in stadium tragedy probe.

text.p: Guatemalan prosecutors said on Wednesday they were counting ticket stubs from last week's soccer game where 81 people were trampled to death in a tragedy blamed on crowding in the stadium.
Prosecutors and other investigators believe one cause of the worst disaster in World Cup history was crowding caused by the oversale of official tickets or by the wholesale forging of tickets.

Nineteen ticket-stub boxes from different entrances to the stadium were taken by authorities after the disaster. Prosecutors unsealed the boxes on Wednesday and began a ticket count, but said they did not know when they would have results.
"This is to determine the number of tickets and verify their authenticity, to see if there are some false tickets," special prosecutor Selvyn Galindo told reporters.

On Oct. 16, half an hour before kick-off of the World Cup qualifying match between Guatemala and Costa Rica in Mateo Flores stadium, an unknown event in the packed, standing-room only terraces at one end of the stadium triggered a human avalanche.
The official death toll, which has varied from 80 to 83, was revised to 81 on Wednesday, the Interior Ministry said.

Galindo said prosecutors planned a dozen other specific steps in their investigation, including interviews on Thursday and on Friday with many of the 147 people who went to hospital because of injuries caused in the stadium disaster.

Three separate groups are investigating the disaster: the team of prosecutors from the attorney general's office, a presidential commission scheduled to release a report later this week, and a congressional commission.
